summary: Provision delegated onboarding bot + topic-aware Slack channel provisioning with gated Confluence seed
description:
Issue summary:
We need a delegated onboarding bot and a topic-aware Slack channel provisioning flow that automatically seeds a Confluence 'micro-space' with a templated runbook and sets timebound retention. The goal is to reduce manual infra requests for new pods and standardize security/compliance metadata at creation time.

Impact:
Currently new team leads open ad-hoc INT requests to create channels, Confluence pages, and Jira projects. This is high-touch for Internal Support and slows ramp for small pods. Standardizing the flow will reduce queue churn and ensure required tags (data classification, owner, retention) are set at creation.

Request (what success looks like):
- A Slack app/bot that can be called via a slash command (/bootstrap-pod) or a lightweight web UI available to team leads.
- Bot provisions Slack channel(s) with topic-driven naming and metadata prompts (data classification, owner, duration).
- On approval, the bot creates a Confluence micro-space from an approved template (runbook + onboarding checklist) and attaches the new Slack channel + a Jira project skeleton.
- All created artifacts must have SSO group ACLs applied and timebound archival/retention triggers.
- An audit event logged to internal Audit Confluence/Jira and an owner notification to #platform-onboarding.

Background/constraints:
- Compliance requires an explicit data_classification field on every new space. Retention policy default for ephemeral experiment pods is 90 days (configurable).
- Must integrate with existing RBAC directory (Okta groups) and create group claims rather than invite users directly.
- Templates live in Confluence page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Onboarding+Microspace+Templates (read-only to support team).
- Prefer serverless lambda for the provisioning webhook; keep infra minimal and observable.

Non-goals:
- This ticket is not for an enterprise-wide self-service portal; scope is internal pod onboarding only (small teams, experimenters).

Priority rationale:
P2 because it improves operational efficiency but does not block production services.
investigation_notes: Spoke with Platform Eng (2026-03-06) — API limits for Slack app are 50 channel creations per minute; safe for pilot.
Checked Confluence API quotas and template permissions; template exists but is currently restricted to admins; request: grant bot service account 'Add' on the template folder.
RBAC: Okta service account needs 'directory.read' and group:create to generate namespace-scoped groups.
Compliance: retention APIs require creation of a label 'ephemeral-90d' or explicit archive date field when creating the space.
